title: Annotatio IV §.XII open: Eighth century — Mejerus age of wrath; images and Eucharistic mutation
pass_a_gloss: §. XII. For the rest, the EIGHTH AGE, which together with the Seventh the aforesaid Mejerus most rightly calls an Age of divine wrath, at the beginning of his ninth Section p. 177, is infamous both by the defense of Images in temples and sacred oratories and by the mutation of Eucharistic truth into falsehood — that is, of bread and wine into the Body and Blood of Christ — each resting on arguments owed solely to false reason and human Wisdom, and moreover by many inventions and fictions of mortals who seemed wise to themselves, both in Doctrine and in rites (on which see our Spanheim, Hist. Imag. Sect. I. §. XI. p. 33).
pass_b_english: §.XII: the EIGHTH age — with the Seventh, Mejerus’s age of divine wrath — is infamous for defending images in temples and for mutating Eucharistic truth into falsehood.
Bread and wine into Body and Blood, each propped on false reason and human wisdom, plus many mortal inventions in doctrine and rites (Spanheim, Hist. Imag.).
source_text: §. XII. Ceterum OCTAVUM SECULUM, quod unà cum Septimo, divinæ iræ Seculum rectissimè appellitat prædictus Mejerus, initio Sectionis suæ nonæ p. 177, Uti Imaginum in templis & oratoriis sacris defensione, ita & veritatis Eucharisticæ in falsitatem, id est, panis & vini, in Corporis & Sanguinis Christi, immutatione, utrâque argumentis rationi falsæ & Sapientiæ humanæ unicè debitis, innixâ, quin multis præterea, tam in Doctrina, quàm in ritibus, sapientium sibi visorum mortalium inventis commentisque, famosum est (Quo de videatur Spanhemius noster, Hist. Imag. Sect. I. §. XI. p. 33.)
